units.source_text: 是年十一月，玉鬘居然生了一个非常可爱的男孩。

en.t: In November of that year, Tamakazura unexpectedly gave birth to a very lovely boy.

units.source_text: 髭黑大将觉得如意称心，欢喜无量，便尽心竭力地爱护这母子二人。

en.t: General Higekuro felt that everything had turned out just as he wished, and in boundless joy he devoted himself completely to cherishing both mother and child.

units.source_text: 此中消息，不须作者缕述，读者自能想见。

en.t: There is no need for the author to describe all that passed between them in detail; the reader can easily imagine it.

units.source_text: 父亲内大臣看见玉鬘的宿运自然地亨通起来，不胜欢喜。

en.t: Her father, the Minister of the Interior, saw Tamakazura's destined fortune naturally opening into prosperity, and was overjoyed.

units.source_text: 他觉得玉鬘的容姿不亚于他所特别钟爱的长女弘徽殿女御。

en.t: He felt that Tamakazura's beauty was in no way inferior to that of his eldest daughter, the Kokiden Consort, whom he especially cherished.

units.source_text: 头中将柏木也把这位尚侍看作可爱的妹妹，对她十分亲睦。

en.t: Kashiwagi, the Captain Secretary, also regarded this Naishi no Kami as a beloved younger sister and was very close to her.

units.source_text: 但因过去曾经误解，不免犹怀妒意，总以为应该入宫伺候皇上才有意义。

en.t: Yet because of his former misunderstanding, he could not help still feeling some jealousy, and he kept thinking that it would only have meaning if she entered the palace and served the Emperor.

units.source_text: 他看见了玉鬘新生儿的美貌，说道：“皇上至今未有子女，正在悲叹。

en.t: When he saw the beauty of Tamakazura's newborn child, he said, "The Emperor still has no children and is grieving over it.

units.source_text: 若能替他生一皇子，面目何等光彩！”

en.t: If she could have borne him an imperial prince, how brilliantly her honor would have shone!"
This was truly a needless thought.

units.source_text: 玉鬘住在家里，亦可如法办理尚侍的公务，故入宫之事，已作罢论。

en.t: Since Tamakazura could properly carry out the duties of Naishi no Kami while living at home, the matter of entering the palace had already been abandoned.
This arrangement, too, was quite reasonable.
